column6: You are responsible for your life. You can’t keep blaming somebody else for your dysfunction. Life is really about moving on!

column8: Very popular Gandhi attribution; look for a primary source in his writings or note if it is unverified.

column6: View your life from your funeral, looking back at your life experiences, what have you accomplished? What would you have wanted to accomplish but didn’t? What were the happy moments? What were the sad? What would you do again, and what you wouldn’t?
column8: Check whether this exercise appears in Frankl's works (e.g. Man's Search for Meaning) or is a paraphrase/misattribution.

column6: Happiness is not something ready made. It comes from your own actions.
Happiness is like being cool - the harder you try the less it's going to happen. So stop trying. Start living.
Most people would assume my business success, and the wealth that comes with it, have brought me happiness. But I know I am successful, wealthy, and connected because I am happy.

column6: Happiness is not a destination, it's a journey. Happiness is not tomorrow, it is now. Happiness is what you are, not what you have.
column8: Check source; similar lines are attributed to several speakers.

column6: The biggest challenge in the world is to be yourself... and to be happy with that. Happiness is the ultimate success.

column8: Check whether James Clear actually wrote this (his site/newsletter) or it is misattributed.

column6: We are not happy, technically speaking, unless we see ourselves progressing - and the very idea of progression implies value.

column8: Often attributed to Depp about buying a private island; a very similar line is attributed to David Lee Roth. Do not discuss his court cases or relationships.

column6: I wake up every morning believing today is going to be better than yesterday.
